label: Logical conventionalism: rule correctness versus truth-directed application and authority
summary: Scoped analyst investigation continuing #1989/#932 and reusing #1084. At fixed interpreted contents and admitted cases, assent and permitted transformation do not suffice for competent actual rule application or soundness. A Boolean affirming-the-consequent countervaluation, incompatible unrestricted implicit-definition rules and their deletion controls, and an incomplete-data rule-application classifier witness distinguish stronger from modest readings; the finite enumeration passed in Python, not Lean. Existing interpretation-regress and all-premise generated-warrant results isolate the iterative and inductive assumptions; neither refutes primitive practice/grasp or infinitism without a further entitlement bridge. Existing K3/LP shared-closure results retain indexed closure and countervaluations. Local authority can grant F6 and withhold preference-independent force; a claim to bind a nonadopting recipient conflicts with its own local-only reason condition only when scope and reason relation match. Full findings, exact dependencies, countermodels and local commands: docs/notes/logical-conventionalism-932.md. No new source claim, graph edge or closure status. Draft, unreviewed.
blocker: whether full norm-governed constitutive practice supplies determinate truth-directed rule application independent of current assent, and whether reason transfers across frameworks independent of uptake. The tests establish neither metaphysically nonconventional grounding nor categorical authority; no new corpus theorem is registered.

current_assessment.scope: Logical conventionalism only: fixed-content preservation, correct application, justificatory regress and authority beyond an adopted framework (#1989/#932/#1084).
current_assessment.assessment: Proposed, unreviewed. Bare assent and arbitrary permissions fail the fixed-content tests. Constrained implicit definition, primitive constitutive practice and indexed validity remain serious accounts; they preserve determinate application and preservation standards not fixed by each particular act of assent. Their ultimate convention-independent origin is unresolved. F1's full intended semantic reading is not established by these local tests; thin F6 can coexist with local reasons and the existing preference-independent authority gap. No new premise discharge or rival-defeat status.
